title: Investor Reporting for Loan Portfolios, Explained | Veteran Loan Servicing
description: What investor and lender reporting should include for a serviced commercial loan portfolio, and why a reconcilable trail matters for LPs and examiners.
h1: Investor reporting for loan portfolios, explained
lede: Investors and LPs do not just want a monthly statement — they want numbers that reconcile to the underlying transactions. Here is what good servicing reporting looks like.

sections.heading: What reporting should include
paragraphs: At minimum, portfolio-level and loan-level status, payment and disbursement activity, delinquency flags, and the ability to trace any reported figure back to the transactions behind it.

sections.heading: Why 'reconcilable' matters
paragraphs: When reporting is produced from the same ledger that runs collection and disbursement, the numbers tie to real transactions. When it is re-keyed into a separate spreadsheet, it drifts — and that drift is exactly what an examiner or LP audit surfaces at the worst time.

sections.heading: Reporting as a diligence asset
paragraphs: A servicer that can answer 'show me' quickly turns an LP or examiner request into a straightforward pull. That capability is itself part of what a lender is buying.

faqs.a: On a regular schedule agreed with the lender; the underlying transaction trail is retained and available on request.

faqs.q: Do you publish portfolio performance numbers publicly?
faqs.a: No. We do not publish assets under management, loan counts, or performance statistics; reporting is delivered privately to each lender for their own book.

ctaBody: Request a walkthrough of the reporting pack and the trail behind it.
